chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"The fasting for the expiation of an oath in al-Zihar is two consecutive months, and consecutiveness is that he fasts one month and fasts some days or a portion of the other month; if something occurs that causes him to break the fast, he breaks it, then makes up what remains of it; and if he fasts one month, then something occurs and he breaks the fast before fasting anything from the other month, so they are not consecutive, then he must repeat the entire fasting."
And he said: "The fasting of three days in the expiation of an oath must be consecutive and they are not separated."

Al-Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: If he intentionally breaks the fast after having fasted some part of the second month, he has erred, and the building is upon what has passed being completed entirely.

key_terms.اَلْبِنَاءُ عَلَى اَلْمَاضِي: Building upon what has passed (maintaining the validity of previous days)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for consecutive fasting in expiation if the fast is broken?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* details the jurisprudential nuances of consecutive fasting (tatābuʿ) for expiating oaths and zihar, distinguishing between valid interruptions that preserve continuity and intentional breaks that require restarting. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the strictness of consecutiveness in expiatory acts, where even partial completion is insufficient if the sequence is fundamentally broken by intent. The ruling underscores the balance between divine mercy for valid excuses and the rigor required for fulfilling religious obligations.
